thread: We deleted our staging environment last month. It was catching about one bug a quarter and costing four figures a month in cloud spend and maintenance.
The problem with staging is that it is never actually like production. Different data, different scale, different traffic. Bugs that matter do not show up there.
What replaced it: feature flags, and shipping to 2% of real traffic first. Same safety, real data, and we find things staging never would have.
The migration took a week. Most of it was moving the two integration tests that genuinely needed a full environment into ephemeral containers in CI.
If your staging environment catches real bugs, keep it. Ours had quietly stopped years ago and nobody had checked.
